query: FeCoNi is an fcc alloy with high saturation magnetization and a low coercive field. Earlier studies examined the high-entropy alloys FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt, but both exhibited soft ferromagnetism. A qualifying high-entropy alloy must have an almost equiatomic multicomponent composition and configurational entropy of at least 1.0R. Subject to these constraints, what single intervention could produce a FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy with greater coercivity than the prior derivatives? Present one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to an appropriate FeCoNi-based baseline, defines the conditions over which it should apply, cites supporting observations from earlier work, and proposes a discriminating experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Adding Al as a fourth, near-equiatomic principal element and giving a medium-temperature anneal will convert a single-phase FCC FeCoNi alloy into a dual-phase high-entropy alloy (HEA) containing coherent B2-ordered nanoprecipitates; these precipitates and the attendant lattice distortion will raise the room-temperature coercive field by roughly an order of magnitude (≥ 3×) relative to otherwise-equivalent FeCoNi-based HEAs that lack Al or B2 ordering.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic Fe20Co20Ni20 solid solution produced by arc-melting and homogenised at 1000 °C, exhibiting a single FCC phase, grain size ≥10 µm, saturation magnetisation ≈1.5 T and coercivity Hc ≈20–40 Oe at 300 K.
generation.intervention: Substitute one quarter of the atomic fraction with aluminium to form an equiatomic quaternary Fe25Co25Ni25Al25 high-entropy alloy (ΔS_conf = R ln 4 ≈ 1.386 R) and anneal at 600 °C for 3 h followed by water quenching.
generation.conditions: Processing window 550–650 °C, 1–4 h, inert atmosphere; grain size kept ≤10 µm. Measurements at 300 K in fields up to 2 T.
generation.structural_mediator: Nanoscale (5–20 nm) B2-ordered Fe–Al–rich precipitates coherently embedded in the FCC matrix together with increased average lattice distortion from the large atomic-size mismatch introduced by Al.
generation.mechanism: 1) B2 nanoprecipitates possess higher magnetocrystalline anisotropy than the surrounding FCC matrix. 2) Their coherent strain fields and interphase boundaries act as strong domain-wall pinning centres. 3) The combined increase in local anisotropy and pinning raises the field required to reverse magnetisation (Hc) while leaving the exchange-dominated saturation magnetisation largely intact because Al is non-magnetic but occupies only one quarter of the lattice sites.
generation.predicted_outcome: Hc of the FeCoNiAl HEA ≥ 120 Oe (≥ 3× higher than the ~40 Oe typical for equiatomic FeCoNi-based soft HEAs such as FeCoNiPd or FeCoNiPt) with Ms ≥ 1.3 T (no more than ~15 % loss relative to the FeCoNi baseline).
generation.baseline: Equiatomic FeCoNiPd (or FeCoNiPt) HEA processed identically but without Al, exhibiting Hc ≈40 ± 10 Oe and Ms ≈1.5 T at 300 K.
generation.boundary: The coercivity enhancement is expected only when: (i) Al content is 15–30 at.% so that B2 ordering occurs; (ii) anneal temperature stays below ~700 °C (above which B2 dissolves); (iii) grain size <20 µm to avoid dominant magnetisation rotation; (iv) measurements are made at or below 400 K (above which thermal activation may overcome pinning). Outside these limits, Hc should revert toward the soft-magnetic baseline.
generation.uncertainty: Exact Hc increment depends on precipitate size/distribution; predicted 3–10 × gain (to 120–400 Oe) carries ±50 % uncertainty. Excessive Al or over-annealing could reduce Ms or eliminate B2 ordering, respectively.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two alloys by identical arc-melting and drop-casting routes: (A) Fe25Co25Ni25Al25 and (B) Fe25Co25Ni25Pd25 (control). Homogenise both at 1000 °C/1 h, water-quench, then anneal 600 °C/3 h. Characterise phase constitution (XRD for FCC and B2 superlattice peaks), microstructure (TEM for precipitates, grain size) and magnetic properties (hysteresis loops by VSM).
measurements: XRD detection of B2 superlattice reflections
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if (i) XRD and TEM show no B2-ordered nanoprecipitates in alloy (A), or (ii) the measured Hc of alloy (A) is ≤100 Oe or not at least three times greater than that of control alloy (B) under identical test conditions.
